prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance–Outbound Load Control Desk handoff, excluding aircraft loading; safety/accuracy/throughput/cutoffs; no explicit modes.
Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) maintains identity/timing/routing; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory to Baggage Control System (Velvet), providing destination/service-date validation. Velvet records assignments/screening/release; validates current routes/cutoffs/allowances before disposition. Pre-cutoff assignments persist unless reassessment required; pending screening blocks induction/build; missed cutoffs require recovery/reassignment.
Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit accepts/stages without reassociation; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk for authorized confirmation. Bag Tag Printer produces durable unique passenger/flight tags and Calibration Witness Tag; replacements require authorized confirmation. Maintenance Technician reports restrictions; verifies witnessed calibration before equipment return.
Transfer Bag Feeder records/meters arrivals without bypassing checks; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station, which records flight matches, flags discrepancies, sends Bag Match Query.
Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns lanes, controls induction, produces Recovery Route Card; applies authorized routes without screening bypass. Induction Tray Conveyor meters/scans/spaces priority bags; jam/open-door/downstream-unready interlocks stop feed.
North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) captures readable tag/image records; South Gate Scanner produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Image Resolution Desk presents images/exceptions; Operator checks features/tag/handling, legibility, approved rescan; inconclusive images require physical inspection with attached-tag/identity agreement. Mismatches remain held pending authorized resolution/escalation.
Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity, sorts authorized destinations/status, sends Chute Occupancy Note; holds unresolved dispositions. Secondary Inspection Chute segregates/retains bags for examination. Security Duty Manager resolves holds; Explosives Response Team examines, produces Custody Seal Log; return requires identity/outcome/authorization agreement.
East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor meter allocations. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) checks order/positions/clearance/window/capacity; receives Carousel Release Slip from Airline Ramp Coordinator checking positions/flights/staffing/equipment/sequence/constraints.
Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) receives isolation notices; coordinates recovery; approves escalated dispositions/window-compliant releases. Velvet authorizes original-path return after checks; revised assignments require approval. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms eligibility/reconciles closeout. Blocked releases prohibited.

New part:
S178: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S179: Safe operation depends on keeping people clear of moving equipment and maintaining a controlled path for every bag.
S180: The Baggage Operations Supervisor may stop induction when an unsafe condition, uncertain bag location, or loss of control is reported.
S181: A stop command places the affected equipment in a defined safe state without disabling unrelated routes that remain safe to operate.
S182: Before entering a conveyor or sorter hazard zone, the Maintenance Technician isolates the relevant energy sources and verifies that movement has stopped.
S183: Guards and access panels remain in place during operation, and bypasses are permitted only under an approved maintenance procedure.
S184: The Baggage Operations Supervisor uses the occupancy note to confirm that a chute can safely accept bags.
S185: The Maintenance Technician consults the Recovery Route Card before returning equipment to service after a route change.
S186: Pebble secures the response area and directs handling of any bag referred for explosives assessment.
S187: The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.
S188: A scanner fault requires the affected feed to be held until the fault is assessed and the bag disposition is known.
S189: The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
S190: Lantern supplies current flight data so that operating routes can be checked against active assignments.
S191: The Baggage Control System records equipment alarms and presents the affected route for review by authorized personnel.
S192: When the Induction Tray Conveyor stops unexpectedly, staff prevent further bag entry and keep the approach area clear.
S193: The Maintenance Technician removes a jam only after confirming isolation and arranging safe access to the blockage.
S194: The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification when a bag's location or identity is uncertain after an interruption.
S195: East Make-Up Conveyor runs only after its guards are confirmed closed and its downstream capacity is available.
S196: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is held from receiving bags when its discharge area is obstructed or its operating status is uncertain.
S197: The Maintenance Technician performs corrective work and reports any condition that prevents safe restart.
S198: The Baggage Operations Supervisor controls the operational hold, communicates its scope, and confirms that affected staff understand the restriction.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
